### Executive Summary
- Multiple **actively exploited zero-days** hit common perimeter/email appliances: **Fortinet FortiMail (CVE-2026-104286)**, **Citrix NetScaler ADC/Gateway (CVE-2026-88771/88772)**, and **Cisco Catalyst SD‑WAN Manager (CVE-2026-76504)**—treat as **internet edge emergency patch/mitigate**.
- Ransomware activity remains tightly coupled to **exploitation of enterprise collaboration platforms** (notably **SharePoint**) and rapid post-exploitation credential/access abuse.
- New reporting highlights a **Microsoft 365-native C2 backdoor** pattern (Outlook/OneDrive as C2), increasing the need to monitor M365 audit signals for “legit-looking” abuse.

---

### High-priority items (immediate attention)

**1) Fortinet FortiMail zero-day (CVE-2026-104286) — KEV / active exploitation**
- **What happened:** Fortinet disclosed a critical FortiMail flaw enabling **unauthenticated arbitrary file write**, confirmed exploited in the wild and added to **CISA KEV**.
- **Why it matters operationally:** FortiMail commonly sits at the **email security perimeter**; compromise can enable mail flow manipulation, credential theft staging, or pivoting into internal networks.
- **Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today:** Confirm asset exposure (internet-facing FortiMail) + patch/mitigate per vendor; hunt last 7–14 days for unusual **admin changes/config exports/new files/web requests** on FortiMail and escalate any anomalies.

**2) Citrix NetScaler ADC/Gateway RCE zero-days (CVE-2026-88771, CVE-2026-88772) — exploited pre-patch**
- **What happened:** Two critical NetScaler RCEs reported as **actively exploited**; Citrix confirmed exploitation occurred before fixes; also added to KEV (per reporting).
- **Why it matters operationally:** NetScaler is frequently a **remote access / app delivery** choke point; exploitation often leads to **credential access + session hijack + lateral movement**.
- **Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today:** Identify all NetScaler instances and apply emergency updates/workarounds; review VPN/ADC logs for **new admin sessions, suspicious endpoints/URIs, config changes, unexpected outbound connections** and isolate affected appliances if suspected.

**3) Cisco Catalyst SD‑WAN Manager auth bypass zero-day (CVE-2026-76504) — KEV / active exploitation**
- **What happened:** A critical **authentication bypass** in Cisco Catalyst SD‑WAN Manager is reported exploited in the wild and flagged by CISA.
- **Why it matters operationally:** SD‑WAN Manager compromise can yield **network-wide control** (routes/policies/telemetry), enabling large-scale disruption and stealthy traffic interception.
- **Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today:** Verify whether SD‑WAN Manager is exposed and patch immediately; hunt for **new admin users/API token creation, atypical management logins, sudden policy/template pushes**, and anomalous device re-registrations.

**4) SharePoint exploitation leading to Warlock ransomware deployments (Storm-2603 / “Longlegs”)**
- **What happened:** Reporting indicates continued exploitation of **Microsoft SharePoint Server vulnerabilities** to deploy **Warlock ransomware**, impacting multiple sectors/regions.
- **Why it matters operationally:** SharePoint is a high-value internal service; exploitation frequently enables **webshells, domain compromise, and rapid ransomware staging**.
- **Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today:** Validate SharePoint patch posture and internet exposure; hunt IIS/SharePoint telemetry for **webshell-like artifacts, unusual POSTs to layouts/handlers, suspicious child processes (w3wp spawning cmd/powershell)** and isolate impacted servers fast.

**5) “Antino” Windows backdoor using Microsoft 365 (Outlook/OneDrive) as full C2**
- **What happened:** Malware campaign described using **Outlook messages and OneDrive files** for command/tasking and data movement (M365 as the C2 fabric).
- **Why it matters operationally:** Blends into normal SaaS traffic; may evade network controls and look like legitimate user activity unless correlated with endpoint and M365 audit data.
- **Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today:** Prioritize detection of **suspicious Office/OneDrive process behavior** on endpoints; in M365, review high-risk users for **unusual mailbox access patterns, odd OneDrive file churn, impossible travel, and new OAuth/app consent**.

---

### Monitoring & detection recommendations
- **Internet edge exploit attempts (FortiMail/NetScaler/SD‑WAN):** Monitor WAF/reverse-proxy, appliance HTTP access logs, and firewall for spikes in 4xx/5xx, suspicious URIs, and new outbound beacons from appliances (ATT&CK: **T1190 Exploit Public-Facing App**).
- **Privileged access changes on appliances:** Collect/alert on new local users, role changes, API token creation, config export/import, and scheduled tasks on Fortinet/Citrix/Cisco managers (ATT&CK: **T1098 Account Manipulation**, **T1136 Create Account**).
- **SharePoint post-exploitation:** From Windows EDR + IIS logs, hunt for `w3wp.exe` spawning `cmd.exe/powershell.exe/rundll32.exe`, creation of new `.aspx`/unknown DLLs in web dirs, and suspicious outbound from SharePoint servers (ATT&CK: **T1505.003 Web Shell**, **T1059 Command and Scripting**).
- **Ransomware early indicators:** Alert on rapid encryption-like file activity, mass renames, deletion of shadow copies, disabling security tools, and lateral admin tool usage (ATT&CK: **T1486 Data Encrypted for Impact**, **T1562 Impair Defenses**).
- **M365-native C2 abuse:** In M365 Unified Audit Log/Defender for Cloud Apps, monitor anomalous **mailbox item access**, high-volume message drafts/edits, unusual OneDrive upload/download bursts, and new consented enterprise apps (ATT&CK: **T1071.004 Application Layer Protocol: Email**, **T1114 Email Collection**).
- **Zimbra email-borne exploitation risk (CVE-2026-73570):** If any Zimbra present, monitor mail gateway/Zimbra logs for malformed messages triggering server-side execution; increase alerting on unusual Zimbra child processes/network egress (ATT&CK: **T1190**, **T1203 Exploitation for Client Execution**—server-side via crafted email).
- **Exploit/PoC “noise” targeting web apps:** Watch for scanning against CMS/app endpoints (Joomla/GetSimple/WordPress plugins) in edge logs; block/ratelimit where feasible and correlate to vuln footprint (ATT&CK: **T1595 Active Scanning**).

---

### Medium-term follow-ups
- **Patch governance:** Add FortiMail, NetScaler, and Cisco SD‑WAN Manager CVEs to an “edge emergency” program with 24–72h SLAs; validate compensating controls where patching is delayed.
- **Exposure review:** Reconfirm which management planes are internet-reachable (SD‑WAN, ADC, mail security consoles); enforce IP allowlists/VPN-only admin access.
- **Hardening:** Ensure appliance and SharePoint servers forward full audit logs to SIEM; enable command-line auditing / PowerShell logging on key servers for better post-exploit visibility.
- **M365 detections uplift:** Implement/use baseline detections for abnormal mailbox/OneDrive activity and new OAuth app consents; tighten conditional access for privileged accounts.
- **Ransomware readiness:** Validate immutable/offline backups and restoration drills; confirm EDR tamper protection and admin credential tiering (reduce blast radius post-exploit).
- **Vuln intake process:** Several new PoCs dropped (multiple CVEs across common software); ensure vuln management is auto-matching PoC availability to your asset inventory for prioritization (assumption: not all affected products are in our environment).
